dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.summary: A standing view of how much assessment work is in flight right now.

steps.0: Read the counters as a snapshot: they follow the candidates already created by the calling system, not people you invite from here.
steps.1: Open Projects to change what an assessment measures, or Candidates to see where individual people are stuck.
steps.2: A figure that looks wrong is almost always a filter question. Reports is where you narrow it down.

projects.title: Projects
projects.summary: A project is one assessment configuration: what it measures, in which language, and where results are delivered.

steps.0: Create the project and pick its assessment type. Standard measures the competencies of a role; Potential measures only MTG and LAT. This choice is permanent once the project goes live.
steps.1: For a Standard project, choose the role. That decides which competencies the interview covers.
steps.2: Set the webhook URL if the calling system should be notified of progress and results, and the exit URL for where the candidate is sent afterwards.
steps.3: Activate the project. From then on the calling system can mint entry links for it; assessment type and role can no longer change.

participants.title: Candidates
participants.summary: Everyone who has been given an entry link for one of your projects, and where each of them got to.

steps.0: Candidates appear here when the calling system creates them. BEAI never invites anyone and holds no contact details.
steps.1: Follow the status to see progress: waiting, in progress, being evaluated, then completed or failed.
steps.2: A transcript is readable from "being evaluated" onward; the scored report only once the candidate is completed.

reports.title: Reports
reports.summary: Every completed evaluation, and the BARS scores behind it.

steps.0: Narrow the list first: project, assessment type, role and period all combine, and the counter shows how many filters are active.
steps.1: Open an evaluation to see each competency, its indicator scores and the verbatim excerpts they came from.
steps.2: Check reliability before comparing two candidates. A low value means much of the interview gave nothing to score, not that the person scored badly.

settings.title: Settings
settings.summary: Your organization, the credentials other systems use to reach BEAI, and who on your team can sign in.

steps.0: Organization profile carries your name; the slug identifies your tenant and cannot change.
steps.1: API keys are for other systems, not people. Grant only the abilities that system actually needs, and copy the key immediately: it is shown exactly once.
steps.2: Webhook defaults apply to projects that do not set their own.
steps.3: Users and roles controls who can sign in to this backoffice, and what they may change.

avatarTemplates.title: Avatar templates
avatarTemplates.summary: The reusable voice and appearance settings an interview runs with.

steps.0: A template belongs to one service, and the service cannot be changed afterwards. Create a new template instead.
steps.1: Leave a setting empty to accept the service default.
steps.2: Templates are configuration, not records: changing one affects every future interview that uses it.

project.definition: One assessment configuration: role, language, competencies and delivery settings.

participant.definition: A person given an entry link for a project. Created by the calling system, never here.

assessmentType.definition: Standard scores the competencies of a role. Potential scores only MTG and LAT, from four fixed questions. Permanent once live.

roleCode.definition: ICO, FLL, MLL, BUL or SRX. Determines which competencies the interview covers.

frameworkVersion.definition: The competency catalogue a project was created against. Pinned at creation, so a later revision never rescores a live project.

lifecycle.definition: Waiting, in progress, being evaluated, then completed or failed. Reading rights depend on it.

ssoLink.definition: The short-lived personal link a candidate uses to start. Minted by the calling system through the API.

bars.definition: Behaviourally Anchored Rating Scale. Each answer is matched against written reference behaviours and scored 1, 3 or 5 — never a value in between.

competency.definition: One assessed capability. Its score is the average of the indicators that could actually be scored.

reliability.definition: The share of indicators the interview produced evidence for. Low reliability means thin evidence, not a low score.

apiKey.definition: A credential for another system. Shown once, at creation, and never retrievable again.

ability.definition: One permission on an API key. A key can do only what its abilities allow.

webhook.definition: An address BEAI calls to report progress and results. Signed, and retried if it fails.

avatarTemplate.definition: Reusable voice and appearance settings for the interviewer.
